question: As the temperature increases, the kinetic energy of particles of matter ______
solution:
The Correct answer is __**increases**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **kinetic energy** of particles is directly proportional to the **temperature** of the matter. As temperature increases, the particles of matter gain more energy and move faster.
 
• Increased temperature leads to an increase in the **vibrational, rotational, and translational motion** of particles, which directly contributes to higher kinetic energy.
 
• This principle is derived from the **Kinetic Molecular Theory**, which states that the temperature of a substance is a measure of the average kinetic energy of its particles.
 
• For example, when water is heated, the molecules move faster, transitioning from a liquid to a gaseous state as the temperature increases.
 
• Temperature increases also cause a change of state (solid to liquid, liquid to gas) due to the higher energy levels of particles overcoming their intermolecular forces.
 
• This concept is fundamental in understanding phenomena such as **thermal expansion, phase changes, and heat transfer.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Becomes zero**__

 __
 
• The kinetic energy of particles becomes zero only at **absolute zero temperature (0 Kelvin or -273.15°C)**, which is theoretically the lowest possible temperature where all molecular motion ceases.
 
• This concept is based on the laws of thermodynamics and is practically unattainable.
 
 
 
• **Decreases**__
 __
 
• The kinetic energy of particles decreases only when the temperature of a substance is **lowered**.
 
• This happens during processes such as cooling or freezing, where the particles lose energy and move more slowly.
 
 
 
• **Remains the same**__
 
 
• The kinetic energy of particles remains the same only when the temperature of the system is constant, i.e., there is **no heat transfer or energy exchange**.
